_what: Settings of the forwarder's origins (src/forwarder/origins.rs): which browser origin answers with which installation of which account. An account signs one origins row (its own key, `signed_domain` first in the signed bytes so no other signature verifies here) naming each host it answers and the installation (`installation_hex` lowercase hex characters) that host shows. A computer that keeps the account posts the row to the forwarder at /a/<address>/<places relay_path>/<tell_again_path> with its own computer proof; the forwarder keeps it in memory for as long as a computer that keeps the account is live, never on disk. A host is one name under a row of `name_suffixes` (one label, `name_label_pattern`), which the first live account to name it holds until no computer that keeps it is live; or the person's own domain, believed only when the TXT record `proof_label`.<host> that the hosting owner's resolver reads holds `proof_value_prefix` + the account's address. A request whose Host is such a host goes, whole, to the live computer that answers the account, at /a/<address>/<installation_path>/<installation> + its own path and query. `most_origins` bounds the hosts of one row; `most_accounts` the accounts the forwarder keeps rows for; `max_host_bytes` one host. An origin may carry `moved_to`, another host of the same row it was renamed to: a page read (GET or HEAD) of it answers 301 to that host with its own path and query, and other requests are still answered by its installation (old trillion src/public-app-host.mjs:1324). A row stays held for `name_hold_ms` (30 days) after a computer of its account was last seen live, in memory: no other account may name its hosts meanwhile, except a person's own domain that another account proves by its TXT record. `certificate_ask_path` is the forwarder's own path an on-demand TLS terminator in front of it asks with `?domain=<host>` before it makes a certificate: 200 when exactly one live account names the host, 404 otherwise; the forwarder itself keeps no certificate (it stores nothing). `root_account_paths` are the account routes a request names by path alone, with no address (old trillion's byte routes, `/namespace/bytes/<identity>?lease=`: the lease is a run capability whose account the forwarder cannot read): a request on the forwarder's own host at one of them, or below one, is carried whole to the live computer of the forwarder's `TRILLION_MCP_ROOT_ACCOUNT` (`with_root_account`), which refuses any lease it did not mint; with no root account it is 404. A name is refused (`reserved`) when its label is one of `reserved_names` (old trillion src/public-app-names.json `reserved`), holds `--` (the old view separator), or matches `code_pattern` (old src/readable-names.mjs LOOKS_LIKE_CODE: a name never looks like an installation id or a random code).

resolver._what: The resolver a person's own domain is believed by in production (src/forwarder/origin_dns.rs DnsTxt, hickory-resolver, the port of old trillion src/public-app-domains.mjs:61 visibleTxt with no vendor): the resolvers the system names (at most `most_servers`) are asked one TXT question each in turn (plain DNS, UDP, then TCP when the answer was cut short) until one answers, within `wait_ms` in all. Nothing is cached.
